title: Determine whether quest 0.12.0 changed revision scope from workspace-wide to per-task
description: Reported by lore-cli: its test file test/link-quest-race.test.ts fails locally against quest 0.12.0, while the lore-cli CI skips that file so its CI stays green regardless. Hypothesis, unconfirmed and inferred only from that failure: 0.12.0 may no longer treat a revision as workspace-wide (one counter for the workspace) and may count it per task instead. This task determines whether 0.12.0 changed revision scope intentionally or not, reproduces it against the installed 0.12.0 by reading the lore-cli test file by ref, and then either states the intended contract in the docs or fixes the behaviour. Outside the DEC-161 narrow-reads campaign; do not start until picked, and escalate only if it turns out to block quest narrow reads.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Reproduce lore-cli test/link-quest-race.test.ts against the installed quest 0.12.0, reading the test file from lore-cli by ref (never from its working tree), and record the observed revision behaviour on this task.

Record a determination: whether quest 0.12.0 changed revision scope (from workspace-wide to per-task or per-record, deliberately or otherwise) or did not, with the evidence that distinguishes the two.

If the change was intended, the quest contract documentation states the revision scope for 0.12.0 and later; if unintended, either a fix restores the prior behaviour or a follow-up task carrying the reproduction is filed and linked from this one.

plan: 1. Read the live tracker and lore-cli test/link-quest-race.test.ts by ref; record the assertion that encodes the scope assumption.
2. Reproduce the revision behaviour against the installed quest 0.12.0 with a direct two-task measurement (unrelated write vs same-record write, and the guarded round-trip).
3. Trace the observed behaviour to the commit and record that introduced it; determine intended vs unintended and whether the contract documentation states the scope.
4. Report the determination and the LCLI-614 implication to team-lead before changing anything.
implementationNotes:
DETERMINATION (2026-10-06): quest DID change revision scope at 0.12.0 -- from workspace-wide to per-record -- deliberately, and it is documented. It is a FIX restoring the documented contract, not a redesign, so no opum-doc design question arises.

REPRODUCTION, AC1 (run literally). lore-cli test/link-quest-race.test.ts at ref 022bb706, fetched via the GitHub API by ref (never its working tree), executed against the installed quest 0.12.0 (nvm node v24.20.0 bin/quest 0.12.0): 2 pass / 1 fail. The failure is the positive control at line 231, "expect(after).not.toBe(revisions[0])": after an unrelated write to T-2, T-1's viewed revision is UNCHANGED (received == expected == 209632b6acf6354adcd6bf4fc57c6bd5cafbe9d3607802b08f662b55e3ca63c7), so the control fails. The other two cases pass; in particular lore's one-attempt-not-retried decision is unaffected, because it does not decide on revision movement alone.

DIRECT MEASUREMENT, AC1. Two-task workspace on installed 0.12.0: capture T-1 rev a691ab2d..., then edit T-2 only -- T-1's revision is byte-identical (UNCHANGED), while T-2's revision moves. A guarded "task edit T-1 --if-revision <captured>" after the T-2 writes returns exit 0, and the same guard with a now-stale revision returns exit 5 naming actualRevision. So on 0.12.0 the revision is a live per-record hash and the guard round-trips.

ATTRIBUTION, AC2. Introduced by QCLI-310 (Done): PR #415, squash a768210c "fix(QCLI-310): scope --if-revision to the record, not the workspace", contained in v0.12.0 (git merge-base --is-ancestor a768210c v0.12.0). Implementation is src/application/tasks/record-revision.ts: sha256 over the located record {task, location}; task view emits it and the edit guards compare against it. Deliberately NOT narrowed: the repository's internal expectedRevision CAS and edit-batch's data.revision (the workspace revision the batch committed at, pinned since QCLI-122).

INTENT AND DOCUMENTATION, AC3. Intended and documented. CHANGELOG 0.12.0 states the change verbatim and adds "This restores the documented scope rather than changing it" -- QCLI-277's acceptance criteria, the task edit help text, and the release note that introduced the flag all said per-record; only the 0.10.0/0.11.0 implementation was workspace-wide. The shipped 0.12.0 binary's own help states it: "quest help task edit" prints "The precondition is scoped to THAT RECORD (QCLI-310): writing any other task leaves it valid."

IMPLICATION FOR LCLI-614. lore-cli's test/link-quest-race.test.ts line-231 positive control, and its test name "SF1: revision is workspace-wide", encode the old buggy implementation; src/commands/link.ts carries the comment "WORKSPACE-WIDE (measured on 0.10.0 and 0.11.0)". Under 0.12.0+ the control is false by design. The fix belongs to lore-cli (retarget or drop the workspace-wide positive control); its decision logic already declines to decide on revision movement alone. The 0.12.0 changelog names both the link.ts comment and this control. No quest behaviour change is warranted. Reported to team-lead for routing.
finalSummary:
Determination: quest's revision scope DID change at 0.12.0, from workspace-wide to per-record, deliberately and documented. It is a FIX (QCLI-310, PR #415, squash a768210c, contained in v0.12.0) restoring the scope QCLI-277, the task edit help text, and the flag's release note always stated -- not a redesign. No opum-doc design question arises.

Verified three ways. (1) Literal reproduction: lore-cli test/link-quest-race.test.ts at ref 022bb706, fetched by ref (not its working tree), run against the installed quest 0.12.0 is 2 pass / 1 fail -- failing exactly at the line-231 positive control "T-1's viewed revision moved under the T-2 write", where on 0.12.0 it does not move. (2) Direct measurement on 0.12.0, two-task workspace: an unrelated write leaves T-1's revision byte-identical and a guarded edit of the untouched T-1 still returns exit 0, while the same guard with a now-stale revision returns exit 5 naming actualRevision. (3) The shipped 0.12.0 binary's own help states "The precondition is scoped to THAT RECORD (QCLI-310): writing any other task leaves it valid", and the 0.12.0 changelog documents the change and calls it a restoration of the documented scope.

Implication: lore-cli's positive control and its src/commands/link.ts comment "WORKSPACE-WIDE (measured on 0.10.0 and 0.11.0)" encode the pre-0.12.0 implementation and belong to lore-cli to update; its decision logic is unaffected. No quest behaviour change is warranted. Reported to team-lead for routing.
